target_customer: Self-storage facility operators, from single sites to multi-facility companies, in the US and Canada
problem: Self-storage operators ran on outdated software and had little online presence, making it hard for customers to find, reserve and pay for units online.
business_model: Free management software with revenue from payment processing fees, plus insurance and a marketplace of units
product_category: Vertical SaaS and payments for self-storage

founders.name: Taylor Cooney
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch says he got the idea after landlords asked him to move out quickly and he struggled to find storage. Little prior storage industry experience.

founders.name: Lucas Playford
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder and COO in the August 2020 release. Not listed on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Web SaaS for reservations, payments and bookkeeping using standard components; payments add compliance work.

defensibility.rationale: Once an operator runs payments and records on the platform switching is costly, but entrenched vendors could add similar features and the product is feature-copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not established by dated sources; the releases only mention unnamed incumbent software providers.

market_need_then: The August 2020 release called OpenUnit the first free management solution for self-storage and described incumbent software as legacy; by May 2021 it had a waitlist of over 800 facilities.

branding.domain_note: Uses openunit.com per the company site.

identity.visual_style: Modern SaaS positioning against legacy software
identity.voice_and_tone: Plain: the modern solution for self-storage facilities

branding.brand_signature: The first free management software for self-storage claim

brand_strength.rationale: Niche industry audience; TechCrunch covered the seed but nothing on the brand itself, and the name is descriptive.

outcome_analysis: OpenUnit is active with a team of about 5 and raised a 150K pre-seed from YC in August 2020 and a 1M seed in May 2021 from Garage Capital, Advisors Fund and Insite Property Group. A free software plus payments model addressed legacy tools in a niche market, and the company also bought the IP of fellow YC company Affiga. No later round is found, so scale beyond early stage is unproven.
notes: Seedtable lists Y Combinator as seed lead, conflicting with TechCrunch and FinSMEs naming Garage Capital, Advisors Fund and Insite. Aggregators report totals between 1.1M and 1.2M. The YC page lists only Taylor Cooney (shown twice); Lucas Playford is from the press release. No competitor source dated near the batch was found; Storable products (SiteLink, storEDGE) existed per undated vendor pages. The 150K pre-seed is the YC deal as described in the company release.
